newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

* A 10 to 4 night curfew will be imposed to secure the site of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum leaders summit one week before it starts on November 25, human rights organizations said. But Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority chairman Richard Gordon maintained that the APEC summit will not affect work, traffic and farming routines in Subic. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- The Philippines on Thursday denied a visa application by East Timorese Nobel peace laureate Jose Ramos-Horta, implementing a ban on him entering the country during November's APEC meeting. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- The families of 105 Filipinos facing death sentences overseas have formed an organisation to lobby the Philippine government to try to save them. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)

* The Energy Department has given Shell Exploration BV of the Royal Dutch Shell group and U.S.-based Occidental Petroleum Co the go-ahead to put up the 80 kilometre onshore pipeline that will transport natural gas from Tabangao, Batangas to other parts of Luzon. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- The Philippine Stock Exchange on Thursday asked the Securities and Exchange Commission to defer the scrapping of the allocation system for initial public offerings until the circular "has been fully explained" to brokers and underwriters. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)
